title: Pairs: the second target
summary: Why the second target of a pair is often missed: transition, recovery and planning the order, plus the cartridge rules for doubles in Sporting™ and Compak® Sporting.

body.html: On a pair (a double) many shooters break the first target and miss the second. The coach then uses two words. The first is transition: moving your eyes, and then the gun, from the first target to the second. The second is recovery: getting the gun and your head back under control after the first shot.

The golden rule is 'eyes first, then the gun'. The eyes leave the broken first clay and find the second; the gun follows. A shooter who watches the first clay break, or swings the gun before finding the second, loses time. Coaches say 'eyes to the second' or simply point.

Recovery: recoil lifts the muzzles and sometimes the head. 'Let the gun recover, then go' means: cheek back down and gun back on line before going after the second target. A good stance with the weight forward makes recovery faster.

Planning: on a simultaneous pair, and on a rafale in Parcours de Chasse – Sporting™, the shooter may take either target first. While reading such a pair, the shooter (in training, with the coach) decides which to take first and where to break it, so the second is easy to find. On a double on report the order is fixed: the call releases the first target, and the shot at it releases the second. Typical phrases: 'take the dropping one first', 'break the first early', 'stick to the plan'. A shooter who changes the planned order on the stand 'went for the wrong one'.

Rules matter here. In Sporting™ the gun position is free between the two targets of any double. The shooter has two cartridges for a double, and both may go at the same target. In Compak® Sporting only one cartridge per target is allowed in a double.
The kinds of doubles and how they are thrown are in Singles and doubles; the rules for doubles are in Doubles: how they are shot and scored.

notes.html: Do not explain penalties yourself: translate the coach and leave rule questions to the referee.

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: Eyes first to the second bird, then the gun.
phrases.meaning: Find the second target with the eyes before moving the gun.

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: Let the gun recover, then go to the second.
phrases.meaning: After the recoil, settle gun and cheek before the second shot.

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.meaning: Shoot first the target that will disappear or fall soonest.

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: Don't watch the first one break.
phrases.meaning: Move the eyes on to the second target at once.

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: You went for the wrong one first, stick to the plan.
phrases.meaning: The shooter changed the planned order of a pair whose order is free; a technique remark, not a rule breach.

key_points.html: Recovery: cheek back on the stock and gun on line before the second target.
Plan the order and break points while reading the pair (in training, with your coach).
Sporting™: free gun position between the targets, and both cartridges may go at one target; Compak® Sporting: one cartridge per target.

quiz.q: What does 'eyes first, then the gun' mean on a pair?

options.text: Close the eyes after the first shot
Look at the barrel before the second shot
Mount the gun before calling for the pair
Find the second target with the eyes first

quiz.explain: In a good transition the eyes lead and the gun follows.

quiz.q: In a Compak® Sporting double, the shooter misses the first target and wants to fire the second cartridge at it too. Is that allowed?

options.text: Yes, the same as in Sporting™
Yes, but only on a simultaneous double
No: only one cartridge per target

quiz.explain: Compak® Sporting forbids doubling the first target in a double; Sporting™ allows both cartridges at one target.

quiz.q: In a Sporting™ double, may the shooter lower the gun between the first and the second target?

options.text: Yes, it is free between the two targets
No, the gun must stay at the shoulder
Only on a double on report
Only if the referee allows it

quiz.explain: The free position applies between the targets of any double, but not before the first one.
